events.excerpt: Summary This proposal introduces post-quantum signature aggregation with leanVM in shadow mode . BLS remains the only authority for aggregates: consensus validity depends on BLS alone, exactly as today. leanVM aggregates and proofs are produced and verified alongside BLS, but their results have no effect on consensus. They are only measured, compared, and reported. When PQ/AI day arrives, an emergency hard fork simply retires BLS and enables leanVM in full. By “PQ/AI day” we mean the point at which quantum computers, or AI-assisted cryptanalysis, make BLS unsafe to rely on. Motivation Ethereum has to be ready for post-quantum signatures well before BLS is actually broken. Waiting until the last moment would mean deploying new, complex code to mainnet in a hurry. Giving leanVM authority early has its own risk: leanVM is new code that hasn’t been tested in production. However carefully it is built and audited, we can’t rule out a soundness bug that accepts an invalid proof, or a liveness bug that rejects a valid one. The main benefit of shadow mode is that Ethereum isn’t put at risk from a leanVM bug before PQ/AI day arrives. Because leanVM has no authority, a leanVM bug can’t break Ethereum’s security or halt the chain. At the same time, leanVM runs on mainnet under real load, so
events.headline: EIP Draft: Run leanVM aggregation in shadow mode alongside BLS until PQ/AI day

Overview Previously, we have presented our analyses of the equilibrium and dynamic simulation of EIP-7999’s multidimensional fee market, comparison with the post-Glamsterdam one-dimensional fee market . In the previous post , we studied three one-dimensional benchmarks: the baseline (64-gas-per-byte floor and CPSB = 1530 ), floor-adjusted + EIP-8368 , and floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 . The strongest is floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 given the current resource demand , which we call the normalized benchmark in the paper: the transaction floor price is adjusted to each propagation allocation, and EIP-8372 scales CPSB and the state gas limit by a common factor, so that regular gas and state gas reach their targets at the same base fee in equilibrium. It keeps the EIP-1559 target-to-limit ratio of 1/2 and the EIP-1559 update rule. events.excerpt: Video game controllers have come a long way from the days when a vibration motor was enough to make the action in the game feel real. Modern controllers can simulate everything from the recoil of a gun to the resistance of pulling a bowstring — but there's still something missing. They can't reproduce the finer details of touching and handling objects in a virtual world. Researchers from Hunan University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences are looking to change that with ElectroPad , a modified PlayStation 5 controller that makes virtual objects feel more realistic. ElectroPad uses a technique called electrotactile stimulation. By sending carefully controlled electrical pulses through electrodes in contact with the skin, it can create localized sensations that mimic textures, edges, and shapes. The idea is to let players feel the surface of a virtual object as their character interacts with it, rather than simply experiencing a generic vibration. To make this possible, the researchers developed a pair of custom covers that fit over the handles of Sony's DualSense controller. Each cover is just 2 millimeters thick but contains 190 individually addressable electrodes, giving the complete controller an impressive 380 stimulation points. events.headline: ElectroPad Makes Virtual Worlds Feel More Real

events.excerpt: Smartwatches are great for keeping important information within reach, but interacting with their tiny touchscreens can be a pain. And when your hands are occupied, tapping a button might not even be possible. Researchers at Northwestern University have developed an alternative that could let you control a smartwatch with simple hand and finger gestures, without ever touching its screen. Their experimental system, called EITWatch , uses electrical impedance tomography (EIT) to detect subtle changes in the muscles and tendons beneath the skin. Unlike previous systems that require specialized wristbands, EITWatch packs its sensing electrodes into an area small enough to fit on the back of a conventional smartwatch. The technology works by passing tiny alternating electrical currents through the wrist and measuring how they travel through the underlying tissues. As fingers move and muscles contract, the electrical impedance of those tissues changes. By analyzing these variations, the system can determine which gesture the wearer is making. The researchers built a prototype around a custom circuit board featuring eight gold-plated electrodes arranged in a 31-millimeter-diameter ring. These electrodes sit against the skin beneath a standard 40-millimeter watch case. The current protot
events.headline: A Smarter Way to Control Your Smartwatch

Today: Layer 2 — decisions without parties. The infrastructure problem (Layer 0) and the identity problem (Layer 1) are hard engineering challenges. Layer 2 — how we actually make decisions — is a different kind of hard. It is not an engineering problem. It is a mechanism design problem, and the failure modes are political. Every democratic system ever built has failed in at least one of the same ways: Token-weighted voting — the wealthy decide. One token, one vote is plutocracy by definition. Simple majority — ignores intensity of preference. A 51% majority with mild opinions overrides a 49% minority whose lives depend on the outcome. Representative democracy — creates permanent political classes who optimise for re-election, not for constituents. Party systems — force multidimensional human preferences into one-dimensional ideological alignments. And in all of the above: the actor with the largest megaphone wins. events.excerpt: IBM has unveiled the Nighthawk r3, an upcoming next-gen quantum processor that will feature 520 qubits, as another step towards a planned fault-tolerant quantum system it hopes to launch in 2029. Big Blue's current Nighthawk r2 was only made available in September and features 120 quantum bits (qubits) capable of handling circuits using 7,500 operations. Its successor, IBM claims, will have more than four times as many qubits and execute 10,000 quantum operations to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the same speed and accuracy. Nighthawk r3 is slated to arrive in 2027, when Big Blue plans to link two of the quantum processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits. IBM said applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, speeding up collection of the millions or billions of samples needed to perform complex computations. Speed determines whether such demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost. The new quantum processor will feature 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers, designed for linking together processors that it will use to enable a single 1,040-qubit system. Rownd 5X unlocks complex geometries with simultaneous five-axis machining, allowing you to reach multiple faces, create intricate contours, and reduce manual repositioning. With better tool access, fewer setups, and greater machining flexibility, you can achieve more in less time. Seamlessly switch between five-axis machining, 3+2 positioning, and three-axis, all in one powerful machine." The Rownd 5X is built around an in-house controller forked from the LinuxCNC project, with an on-board 13.3" touchscreen display.
